newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aerospatiale says talks continue on China plane.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale says talks continue on China plane.

text.p: French aircraft maker SNI Aerospatiale said on Tuesday that talks on terms for building a 100-seater passenger jet with China were continuing and that nothing had been signed.

"The negotiations are continuing on the terms of cooperation, nothing has been signed," a spokeswoman for Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale said in response to a report from the official Xinhua news agency that China would hold a 46 percent stake in the Asia Express 100 project.
Aerospatiale is a member of the Aero International Asia (AIA) joint venture China picked to build the plane.
Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot met Chinese prime minister Li Peng while attending the Zhuhai air show in China, the spokeswoman said.
She could not confirm the Chinese agency report which said AIA would take a 39 percent stake and Singapore Technologies Aerospace 15 percent in the AE-100 project.

Portuguese news agency Lusa earlier reported that China had signed a $1.7 billion agreement with AIA on the plane. The news emerged at the air show held near the Portuguese-administered territory of Macau.
British Aerospace Plc and Alenia, part of Italy's Finmeccanica holding company, are the other AIA members beside Aerospatiale.
China has forecast production of 1,000 AE-100 planes, to be sold mainly to Asian regional carriers. The plane would be built in China, with West European technology.
Aerospatiale wants to base the plane on a cockpit common to the Airbus Industrie family, in which it is a senior partner, along with Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG.
